info.title: Answerline API
info.description:
Answerline tracks how AI assistants and search engines answer, across providers and regions. Each request comes back as structured JSON holding the engine's answer: the parsed text, its cited sources and whatever else the engine returned with them, geo-targeted to a country you choose (which countries are available depends on the engine; see [coverage](/docs/coverage)).

## Authentication

Pass your API key in the header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. You can create keys yourself at https://dashboard.answerline.dev/keys, and each new account begins on a free tier with 500 one-time credits. A single key works for all endpoints; keys cannot currently be limited to particular scopes.

## Versioning and deprecation

The URL path carries the version. All endpoints sit under `/v1/`; no header or query parameter selects a version.

Changes inside a version only add things: new endpoints, optional request fields and response fields may be introduced at any moment. Clients have to skip response fields they don't know. Anything breaking ships under a new path (`/v2/`) and never replaces an existing version.

Deprecation is announced in the endpoint's responses themselves, not just in a changelog: the `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) gives the date it became deprecated, `Sunset` (RFC 8594) gives the date it will stop answering, and the replacement is given by a `Link` header carrying `rel="deprecation"`. For generally available endpoints, those two dates are at least six months apart. No endpoint is currently deprecated.

## Rate limits

Each response reports the current limit state, letting a client pace itself using the response in hand: `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, plus the headers for concurrency and credits. Rate limiting uses a one-second window, so a `429` caused by it goes away almost at once; a `429` caused by the concurrency limit goes away once your running jobs complete. `Retry-After` is not set on either, and no IETF `RateLimit-*` headers are sent.

## Errors

All 4xx and 5xx responses share the `Error` envelope: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details", "timestamp" } }`. Clients should branch on `code`, a stable identifier meant for machines; `message` is meant for people reading logs.

post.description:
Returns the destination URL of a single Google redirect link. Pass the `redirectLink` value that accompanies each resolved link in a Google Search, Google News or AI Mode response; the reply contains the URL it leads to.

Free of credit charges and takes no concurrency slot, but it counts toward the per-second rate limit the same way other calls do. One link is resolved per request, and Google is given up to 10 seconds to respond.

query.description: Query to run on Google. Mandatory when 'url' is not given; send one or the other, never both.

url.description: A full URL of a Google web search, executed as-is in place of a request assembled from 'query' plus the targeting fields. It has to be absolute and http(s), hosted on one of Google's web search domains (google.com, google.co.uk, www.google.de, ...), with '/search' as its path and a 'q' that is not empty. Cannot be combined with 'query', 'location', 'uule' or 'pages', since the URL already determines them. It may carry only these query parameters: 'q', 'gl', 'num' (treated as result depth), 'hl' and 'uule'; a URL with any other (such as 'start', 'tbs' or 'safe') is refused with a 400. A URL containing 'tbm' is refused: it points at a Google vertical that has a separate endpoint and price (for tbm=nws, call POST /v1/monitor/google/news).

country.description: Country for localized search results, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Mandatory in the standard request form. If you send 'url' instead, the country is taken from the URL's 'gl' parameter — set it yourself to override that value, or when the URL carries no 'gl'.

location.description: Location name in Google's canonical comma-separated form 'City,Region,Country' (roughly 100,000 accepted locations are listed at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/data/geotargets). Combine with 'country' to target a specific city. Cannot be sent together with 'uule' — choose one of the two. Not allowed when 'url' is set.

uule.description: A ready-made Google UULE string for exact geo-targeting, in the location-name form (starting w+CAIQICI); the coordinate form (a+) is refused with a 400. Supply it when you already have an encoded UULE rather than a location name. Cannot be sent together with 'location' — pass only one of the two. Not allowed together with 'url'; in that case add 'uule' to the URL's query string.

device.description: Device to run the search on. 'desktop' gives the desktop SERP, while 'ios' (Safari on an iPhone), 'android' (Chrome on an Android phone) and 'mobile' (same as 'android') each give the mobile SERP.

pages.description: How many pages of search results to retrieve (1-10). Not allowed together with 'url' — when 'url' is given, depth is taken from the URL's 'num' parameter (rounded up to full 10-result pages, at most 10 pages).
